title: geogen state declarations v1
description: The `state` section of a manifest or chunk index: every variable of the package with its owner in its key, every interaction as the instance state it is, and the signals and inputs assets offer to wiring. Semantics: docs/rules.md. `variables` and `interactions` are those of a rules program.

package.description: The package the world: and actor: keys and the stable IDs belong to.

variables.description: Declared variables. The key names the owner: '<thing id>#<name>' (one placed instance), 'world:<package>.<name>' (one shared value) or 'actor:<package>.<name>' (one value per actor: the player or an NPC).

interactions.description: Every interaction, keyed '<thing id>#<interaction>'. Its state is a choice over `states` starting at `initial`; '<key>_locked' is its lock, a bool.

duration.description: Seconds from being used or driven to arriving.

when.description: A compiled, resolved condition tree (geogen-condition.v1.schema.json), read with the user as the actor: while it is false, use does nothing (rules still drive it).

refused.description: With `when`: a use it stops is fed back to the user as a notify of this text.

next.description: The state `use` heads to from here; absent: not usable.

then.description: The state it moves on to after arriving.

emit.description: Signal raised from the thing on arrival.

signals.description: Named outputs, keyed '<thing id>#<signal>'. Each is the signal event {type: signal, subject, name, data}. With `from`, the runtime raises it whenever an event matching `from` is processed (as a rule with that `on` and one emit effect would); without, the world raises it: an interaction of the subject emits it, or the subject is an NPC that raises it when an actor greets it.

data.description: The fields the signal's event data carries, by type: rules read them as event.<field>.

inputs.description: Named things a thing accepts, keyed '<thing id>#<input>': driving one sets `set` to `to`, or to the value the driver gives when there is no `to`.

driven.description: Set by the runtime, not by rules: what drives it ('train': true while a train of this service stands at the station, from its timetable; 'place': the number of things a place that detects props has in it).
